title: Algebraic immunity of arbitrary Boolean direct sums
summary: Characterize exactly the algebraic immunity of a Boolean direct sum and when it attains the optimum for its total dimension.

formal_statement.body: Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ and $g:\mathbb F_2^m\to\mathbb F_2$, and define their direct sum by $h(x,y)=f(x)+g(y)$. Determine $\operatorname{AI}(h)$ from the component data and give necessary and sufficient conditions for $$\operatorname{AI}(h)=\left\lceil\frac{n+m}{2}\right\rceil.$$ The characterization must cover every admissible pair $(f,g)$, rather than only sufficient conditions or selected constructions.

scope.domain: Algebraic immunity of direct sums of Boolean functions
assumptions: $f$ and $g$ are Boolean functions on disjoint variable sets
scope.unresolved_remainder: Published later work gives sufficient lower-bound criteria and exact values for selected constructions, but no exact formula and necessary-and-sufficient optimality conditions for every admissible direct sum.
